# fraud-deferral

Pre-registered, delay-aware study of **when uncertainty-based deferral pays** in fraud / illicit-transaction detection under temporal shift.
Code, frozen configurations, pre-registration locks and results for the paper.

**Status: complete. Study 1 and Study 2 are each locked (`results/PREREG_LOCK.txt`, `results/PREREG_LOCK_STUDY2.txt`).**

## Headline results (all numbers are generated by `experiments/make_numbers*.py` from `results/`)
Two separately pre-registered studies. The manuscript and its sources (`paper/`) are not in this repository until publication; the scripts that generate its numbers, tables and figures are.

| Hypothesis | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Study 1 (Elliptic) H1a: MAD beats the Chow control after the regime break | Not supported: gain -30.9 per 1,000, CI [-62.3, -0.3] (excludes zero only before Holm) |
| H1b: any gain is attributable to uncertainty | Not supported |
| H2: uncertainty gain tracks conditional miscalibration | Not supported (rho 0.30, CI [-0.23, 0.72]) |
| H3: graph encoders beat feature-matched baselines | Not supported |
| Study 2 (BitcoinHeist, amount-based costs) S2-H1: Chow band beats a single threshold | **Not supported, reversed**: band 24% more expensive in the primary cell (cheaper in 5 of 9 cells) |
| S2-H2: epistemic cap equivalent to the band | Supported (TOST, 2% margin) |
| S2-H3: MAD vs band (predicted <= 0) | Contrary to prediction: MAD 4.5% cheaper, none of it from its uncertainty cap |
| S2-H4: three novelty-capped policies | No effect |

Consistent finding: ensemble uncertainty and feature-space novelty add no decision value. The review band cuts cost 38% on Elliptic (uniform costs) but fails under amount-based costs, because the score is calibrated on average and not conditional on the amount (post-hoc: stratified recalibration recovers about half the gap).

## Reproduce
```
pip install -r requirements.txt                                   # Python 3.11, optional CUDA (4 GB is enough)
python -m src.data.splits && python -m src.data.download elliptic baf   # needs ~/.kaggle/kaggle.json
python -m src.data.loaders && python -m src.data.validate --baf-variants Base "Variant III"
python -m pytest tests -q && python scripts/check_leakage.py      # 62 tests incl. leakage + mutation-verified guards
# dev era (tuning): src.training.tune, src.training.make_scores <ds> dev main, src.policies.tune_policies <elliptic|baf>
python -m scripts.lock_test                                        # freeze + hash the pre-registration (once)
python -m src.training.make_scores elliptic test all               # test era refuses to run without the lock
python -m src.training.make_scores baf_Base test all; python -m src.training.make_scores "baf_Variant III" test main
python -m experiments.run_policies elliptic test --variants ; (same for baf_Base, "baf_Variant III")
python -m experiments.analyze test elliptic baf_Base "baf_Variant III"
python -m experiments.synth_mechanism ; python -m experiments.error_analysis ; python -m experiments.novelty_probe   # exploratory
python -m experiments.make_numbers && python -m experiments.make_tables && python -m experiments.make_figures
python -m experiments.study2 tune|lock|score|novelty|policies|analyze   # Study 2 (BitcoinHeist from UCI, see data/README.md)
python -m experiments.extra_analyses; python -m experiments.study2_diagnosis; python -m experiments.study2_posthoc   # exploratory
python -m experiments.make_numbers2 && python -m experiments.make_figures2 s1 s2
```
(Windows has no `make`; the targets above are the commands.)

## Layout
`src/data` loaders, maturity access, frozen splits, validation | `src/models` tabular + batched NN/GNN scorers | `src/training` walk-forward driver, tuning, score generation |
`src/calibration` recalibrators | `src/policies` decision policies (incl. MAD) and dev tuning | `src/evaluation` costs, calibration, diagnostics | `src/stats` block bootstrap, tests |
`experiments/` runners, analysis, figures, tables, numbers | `configs/` frozen splits, costs, model and policy hyper-parameters, `preregistration.yaml` | `results/` audits, logs, analysis JSON (score tables are not committed); the manuscript folder `paper/` is local only (the three `make_*` scripts write their numbers and tables into it).

## Non-negotiable rules (enforced by tests)
- Training/calibration labels are read **only** through `src/data/maturity.py`; flipping every immature label must not change any policy decision.
- The scorer trains only on periods <= tau - D - 1 - W_c, so the matured calibration window is out-of-sample for it.
- Splits come only from `src/data/splits.py` (hash-checked); no random split / KFold in `src/`.
- Scalers fit on the training pool only; the clock (`tx_f1`, `month`) is never a feature; graphs are inductive per period.
- Test-era scoring refuses to start without `results/PREREG_LOCK.txt`; every test-era label access is appended to `results/test_touch_log.json`.
